note: One entry per beat group; no (scene, shot) pair repeats. shot_arg = name:seconds stretch for render.mjs/assemble. duration_hint = narration estimate at 150 wpm.

script_lines: With bins. With barriers. With human chains.
shots.visual: gate barricade of wheelie bins + barriers, faceless pupils with readable placards, amber glow on the chained gate

script_lines: And it all started with a few empty classrooms, in one school outside Paris.
shots.visual: drop from high to one amber point at Créteil

script_lines: Why are so many of them ending up hurt, or in custody?
shots.visual: behind pupils toward a shield line in amber haze (replaces the red-tinted 2D silhouette)

script_lines: And can the government calm it down, before the next wave?
shots.visual: calendar rail, 13/17/23/27 Oct and 5 Nov flick past

script_lines: This is what's happening in France's high schools, as of today.
Créteil [kray-TAY]. A suburb just southeast of Paris.
shots.visual: held framing on the Créteil dot

script_lines: Lycée Saint-Exupéry [LEE-say san-teg-zoo-pay-REE]. About fifteen hundred pupils.
shots.visual: night, street level, slow push on the intact façade; LYCÉE lettering warms to amber

script_lines: At the start of this school year, several teaching posts there were simply empty.
shots.visual: dollhouse cutaway, three teacher desks in three rooms light amber one by one

script_lines: So in mid-September, the teachers went on strike.
shots.visual: calendar tile 17 SEPT teachers strike

script_lines: The next day, the pupils joined in, their own way. They blocked the gates.
shots.visual: dawn, bins slide in from the street one after another and build the barricade, amber on the chain

script_lines: A few days later, two MPs from the radical-left party La France Insoumise [lah frahnss an-soo-MEEZ] visited, and posted about it.
Remember that visit. The government will.
shots.visual: two phones with generic post layouts dated 21 SEPT, amber underline

script_lines: Then, on September twenty-fourth, a rap-news outlet called Booska-P [BOO-skah PEE] interviewed eight pupils from the school.
They talked about feeling abandoned, as kids from the banlieue [bahn-LYUH], the working-class suburbs.
On TikTok, the clip was watched around one and a half million times.
shots.visual: blurred faceless vertical video, caption, counter to 1.5M

script_lines: And the idea spread with it. If your school is falling apart... block it.
By September twenty-fifth, around sixty schools in the Paris region were disrupted.
Three days later, the Interior Ministry counted one hundred and eighty, across France.
And on October first... one thousand and twenty-seven.
shots.visual: Créteil → suburbs → cities → 1 Oct flood (labels no longer overlap)

script_lines: Teenagers don't shut down a thousand schools over one viral video.
So what's actually going on inside these buildings?
shots.visual: amber slice line opens the façade into the cutaway

script_lines: Let's walk inside a typical French lycée.
shots.visual: glide through the glass entrance doors into the hall, amber light lands on the stairs

script_lines: First, the building. On average, it's sixty-five years old.
shots.visual: rust streaks and cracks creep over the concrete, one long crack glows amber

script_lines: More than half of France's lycées were built before 1970.
shots.visual: broken toilet block, taped HORS SERVICE stall picked out in amber

script_lines: Pupils describe rats, cockroaches, and ceilings that have come down.
shots.visual: stained ceiling, missing tile, drips, rat

script_lines: In summer, teachers report classrooms at thirty-five to forty degrees. In winter, some rooms have no heating at all.
shots.visual: thermometer climbs to 38 °C in low amber sun

script_lines: A Senate report says fixing them would take about one and a half billion euros a year.
shots.visual: coin stacks 2026→2050, "€1.5 BN needed every year"

script_lines: But for most pupils, the building isn't the biggest problem. It's who's missing from it.
shots.visual: amber pool on an empty teacher desk

script_lines: Fifty-three percent were missing at least one teacher.
shots.visual: empty staff room, blank name tags glow amber

script_lines: But by the ministry's own count, in 2024 to 2025, ten percent of lycée teaching hours simply didn't happen.
shots.visual: timetable, 1 in 10 slots flip to amber gaps

script_lines: And when teachers are there, classrooms are packed. A teacher in Marseille [mar-SAY] says she has thirty-seven pupils in her class.
shots.visual: 37 desks light up one by one, the 37th pupil squeezed in by the board flares last

script_lines: French lycée students also spend around twelve hundred hours a year in class. The average across OECD countries is nine hundred and sixty.
shots.visual: slab stacks 60 vs 48 (×20 h), "+240 h"

script_lines: And at the end of all that, there's Parcoursup [par-koor-SOOP], the national platform that decides who gets into university.
shots.visual: generic admissions dashboard, amber cursor

script_lines: This summer, eighteen percent of applicants got no offer at all in the main round. Two years ago, it was ten.
shots.visual: 100 application cards flip, 18 "NO OFFER"

script_lines: Then, on October first, the government published its budget for 2027.
shots.visual: Assemblée portico at night, budget beat

script_lines: But the same budget cuts one thousand five hundred and eighty-eight teaching posts.
shots.visual: teacher name tags drop out leaving amber gaps

script_lines: The budget landed on the very day the protests hit their most violent point.
shots.visual: calendar 1 OCT tile

script_lines: And that day, the map of France caught fire.
shots.visual: low oblique over France, 180 → 1,027 lycées ignite in a rush

script_lines: Here's how fast it moved.
First, the suburbs north and east of Paris. Saint-Denis. Sarcelles. La Courneuve.
Then Marseille. Lille. Lyon [lee-OHN].
Then Nantes. Rennes. Bordeaux. Toulouse. Strasbourg.
shots.visual: day-by-day flight, named cities light (Saint-Denis … Strasbourg)

script_lines: Two hundred and twenty-two lycées were fully blockaded.
shots.visual: 1,027 dim, 222 turn solid amber

script_lines: In Nantes, a fire destroyed a lycée's entrance hall.
shots.visual: burned entrance hall, soot, tape, embers (generic, no real school)

script_lines: In Marseille, a firefighters' truck was torched, and the city shut down its entire bus and metro network.
shots.visual: burned generic fire truck, bus shelter "NETWORK SUSPENDED"

script_lines: The movement even crossed the border, into schools in Belgium, and then Italy.
shots.visual: amber arcs Lille → Charleroi, Liège (Belgium) and Lyon → Italy

script_lines: On October second, prefects closed around four hundred lycées, and banned gatherings outside them.
The message from the state was clear. Stay home.
shots.visual: ~400 amber padlocks pop over lit lycées

script_lines: The pupils answered with a date. Tuesday, October sixth.
shots.visual: 6 Oct police counts as glowing columns

script_lines: In Lyon, twenty thousand, by police count. In Toulouse, thirteen and a half thousand.
shots.visual: 6 Oct police counts as glowing columns

script_lines: First, the tools.
French police use what they call "intermediate weapons".
shots.visual: three stylised intermediate weapons on plinths

script_lines: The LBD, a launcher that fires rubber projectiles.
shots.visual: LBD with dotted projectile path

script_lines: Launchers that fire tear-gas grenades.
shots.visual: tear-gas launcher, canister arc

script_lines: And dispersal and stun grenades, which explode, some scattering rubber pellets.
shots.visual: grenade, abstract radial pellet burst

script_lines: Then came three cases that changed the conversation.
shots.visual: three amber pins drop: Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône 28 SEPT, Tours 30 SEPT, Lens 5 OCT

script_lines: September twenty-eighth. Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône [san-TWAN loh-MOHN], northwest of Paris. A fourteen-year-old's jaw is broken by a tear-gas round, fired at close range.
shots.visual: launcher with amber CLOSE RANGE bracket

script_lines: September thirtieth. Tours [TOOR]. A sixteen-year-old loses the use of an eye. The prosecutor says it's consistent with an LBD round.
October fifth. Lens [LAHNSS], in the far north. A fifteen-year-old loses his hand to a police grenade.
shots.visual: low flight Tours pin → Lens pin

script_lines: Two days later, Nuñez suspended stun grenades at lycée protests, "until the facts are clarified".
shots.visual: grenade under a glass case, SUSPENDED · 7 Oct

script_lines: But the violence hasn't gone one way.
shots.visual: behind police helmets toward pupils with placards

script_lines: Headteachers have been hit by fireworks.
shots.visual: night, from the yard: a firework streak arcs over the barricade and bursts in sparks

script_lines: So who does the government blame? And what is it actually offering?
Its first answer was political.
shots.visual: Matignon façade, one office window goes amber

script_lines: But the newspaper Le Monde [luh MOHND] read the intelligence note behind that claim.
It covered one area, and a few days. It mentioned outsiders six times. The party, once.
shots.visual: redacted note, "outsiders" ×6 vs "LFI" ×1 highlighted (ILLUSTRATION tag)

script_lines: Three thousand teachers, he said, would arrive within hours.
Three thousand and twenty-four supply teachers, already on the payroll, but not assigned to any classes.
shots.visual: rows of teachers on standby, amber lamps, front rows step forward

script_lines: They're going to the schools hit hardest: a hundred and fourteen "red" lycées, and about four hundred "orange" ones.
shots.visual: 114 red + ~400 orange lycées (official categories)

script_lines: And critics asked the obvious question. If three thousand teachers were available, why weren't they in classrooms already?
shots.visual: teachers descend on amber threads onto red/orange school blocks

script_lines: Then there's the damage. Twenty-four lycées have been burned or ransacked.
shots.visual: ransacked classroom, overturned desks, fire light

script_lines: About thirty thousand pupils have no classes in person.
shots.visual: field of empty desks, one amber hero desk

script_lines: The government's estimate of the bill: at least thirty million euros.
shots.visual: note-brick pile, "≥ €30 MILLION"

script_lines: Anyone in a group that causes damage could be made to pay up to ten thousand euros, even if they didn't break anything themselves.
shots.visual: ten faceless pupils, €10,000 tags drop

script_lines: Right now, the blockades are shrinking.
On October first, more than a thousand lycées were affected. On October ninth, a hundred and forty-one were still closed.
shots.visual: 1,027 lit lycées go dark until 141 remain

script_lines: Here's the calendar.
shots.visual: calendar full wall, NOW line at 11 Oct

script_lines: Tuesday, October thirteenth. A national strike and day of action, called by student and teacher unions.
shots.visual: 13 OCT lights amber

script_lines: Saturday the seventeenth. A separate call that's been spreading on TikTok, from an anonymous account, about fuel prices, housing and discrimination.
shots.visual: phone, anonymous call "SATURDAY 17 OCTOBER"

script_lines: It's not an official union date. But some lycée protesters have said they'll be there.
That same weekend, the autumn school holidays begin. Unions worry two weeks off could drain the movement.
shots.visual: 17 OCT dashed outline + autumn holiday band unrolling

script_lines: October twenty-third. The government's online consultation for pupils closes.
October twenty-seventh. The rioters-pay bill goes to the Senate.
By the end of October, Lecornu has promised decisions, and changes to the budget.
And on November fifth, France's five biggest union confederations strike together, on pay and public services.
shots.visual: END OCT bracket, 5 NOV

script_lines: And behind all of it, a presidential election in April 2027.
shots.visual: rail extends to APR 2027

script_lines: In mid-September, this was about a few empty posts, at one school in Créteil.
Now, it's a question for the whole country.
shots.visual: holds on the Créteil dot, then an amber wave runs over the whole country
